title: Uploading
purpose: The footage leaves every phone and reaches the client, complete and on time. This is the part that lost the most in August.
how: One hour of footage is 5.4 GB. At 1,000 hours a day, that is 5.4 TB a day, and it needs about 500 Mbps of upload speed day and night. Mobile data cannot carry this, so never upload over mobile data.

There are only two ways to upload. The first is the site's own wireless internet: the phones stay at the site and upload there. We test it on launch day, and most sites will not pass. The second is a hub. We have two fiber hubs. The Central hub is at the Central Cairo warehouse and office. The East hub is in 5th Settlement, and we are finding the place this week. A West hub is planned, not live. Until it opens, sites on the west side and 6th of October upload on site or run to Central. Every night a runner takes the site's phones to the nearest live hub. Each hub can take a full day, so one landlord problem or one cut line cannot stop the company.

A place is not a hub until it passes the test: 20 phones uploading for 8 hours at a steady 300 Mbps or better. Coworking spaces say they have "high speed" internet, but that speed is shared, and upload is slower than download. Measure it yourself and do not take their word for it.
The Planning and Logistics Lead owns the hubs, the internet lines, the runners, and the hub attendants. Hub attendants and runners report to the Planning and Logistics Lead, not to Moharam directly.

breaks.do: Send the runs to the other hub. Sites on their own wireless internet are not affected. The backlog rule allows one day. The Planning and Logistics Lead opens a ticket with the ISP right away.

breaks.what: A vehicle is stolen or crashes
breaks.do: Find the phones with MDM and lock them with lost mode. If they do not come back, wipe them. File a police report the same day. File an insurance claim, update the registry, and replace the phones from the 10% spare pool.

Show the letter, the commercial register, and the phone list. Call the Planning and Logistics Lead, then Moharam. Never argue, and never hide the number of phones. If the police keep the phones, Mano brings a lawyer and writes down what happened the same day.
Check storage every time a phone is docked. Swap a full phone for a spare, and flush the full one first. A full phone is the Portfolio Manager's problem and must be fixed tonight.

questions.q: Why not upload over mobile data?
questions.a: The carrier decides how much data it will carry, and at our volume it says no. Fiber is the only path that can grow with us.

questions.q: Why two hubs and not one big one?
questions.a: One hub means one landlord, one line, and one road. A second hub costs less than one lost day in a 25,000-hour month, and it is closer to the sites on its side of the city.

questions.q: A site will not let the phones leave overnight. What do we do?
questions.a: Then the site's wireless internet must pass the test on launch day. If it cannot, tell Moharam before launch. A phone never stays full overnight.

questions.q: Who pays for a site's internet upgrade?
questions.a: Usually we pay, and it is usually cheap. We write it into the site agreement so nobody argues later.

pipeline.hubTest: 20 phones uploading for 8 hours at 300 Mbps or better
pipeline.rule: Never keep more than a day of footage overnight.

paths.name: On-site wireless internet
paths.text: The phones stay at the site and upload there every night. We test the site's wireless internet on launch day: the phones must upload a full day of footage overnight. Most sites will not pass.

paths.name: Fiber at a hub
paths.text: Every other site is a hub site. Every night a runner takes all its phones to the nearest hub in one trip, in the provided bag. Both sides sign at every handover.

hubs.name: Central hub
hubs.serves: Sites in the center of the city. Also the west side and 6th of October until the West hub opens.

hubs.name: West hub
hubs.serves: Sites on the west side and 6th of October, once it opens. Until then they upload on site or run to Central.

transport.text: All of a site's phones go to the hub in one trip, in the provided bag. Nothing is written on the outside.
A printed phone list goes in the bag: device numbers, count, site, time out, and the runner's name. Both sides sign it at every handover.
Every runner carries the company letter in Arabic on letterhead, a copy of the commercial register, the phone list, and two phone numbers that someone will answer.
Both sides sign at pickup and at drop. MDM location tracking is on for every phone while it travels.
Runners never stop on the way.
The morning return is the same runner and the same three sites as the night before, all phones back before 7:00 AM.
A missing runner at end of shift is called by the Planning and Logistics Lead from the spare list before 6:00 PM.

en.title: To whom it may concern
body: {company}, commercial register number {register}, confirms that the person carrying this letter, {runner}, is transporting {devices} mobile phones and their accessories. The phones belong to the company. This person is moving them between the company's work sites and the company's upload facility, as part of the company's video data collection work.
The devices are company property. They are listed on the attached phone list. They are being carried on the company's instructions.
To confirm this at any hour, call {contact1} or {contact2}.

ar.title: إلى من يهمه الأمر
body: تؤكد شركة {company}، سجل تجاري رقم {register}، أن حامل هذا الخطاب، السيد/ {runner}، يقوم بنقل عدد {devices} هاتف محمول وملحقاتها، وهي مملوكة للشركة، بين مواقع عمل الشركة ومقر رفع البيانات الخاص بها، في إطار عمل الشركة في جمع بيانات الفيديو.
الأجهزة ملك للشركة، ومدرجة في البيان المرفق، ويتم نقلها بتعليمات من الشركة.
للتأكد في أي وقت، يرجى الاتصال على {contact1} أو {contact2}.
